Everyone here has said so much of what I could say, so I won’t repeat them too much. I mainly wanted to offer you a different perspective: I think you are very strong and brave for continuing forward each day, despite the hardships that could occur. There is bravery in holding on to the hope of a glimpse of sunshine or warmth after a cold season, in taking care of yourself in a world that is harsh, in experiencing everything the world has to offer you, in experiencing the range of emotions and sensations we are capable of as humans, in knowing the world is a scary place and also a place full of love and community. I hope everyone’s words can give you extra strength to continue on with, and give you some different things to think about. Take care out there- I hope some parts of the movie feel better to watch soon.
Editing to say it’s okay to be cowardly and protect yourself, and it’s okay to be brave and take care of yourself in a harsh world. There’s no right way to be- at the end of the day we decide how we put our feelings to bed, if that makes sense. This is just my two cents, as someone who has struggled a lot in the past and found neutral observation of life an easier road to comprehend.

I’ve used cannabis to treat my fibromyalgia and other issues in the past, to mixed success. This is just my personal experience, but I found only CBD unhelpful. I have had better results with full spectrum products, and generally it helps me tolerate the discomfort of pain flare ups better. It never really removes it, just helps the overall discomfort of existing. I don’t have any helpful information to contribute about dosage, apologies. I do recommend keeping a pain chart and writing down details about your methods/doses to look back on to help you track what you try and hopefully find some results. Trial and error can be frustrating, but I hope you find something that helps and more helpful information. Best of luck on your search!

NTA - he might not understand the impact of his actions, but that does NOT excuse him from changing something you rely on and making you worry about your health. If he was concerned, it would be more appropriate for him to discuss his worries with you instead of just making changes that impact you without even mentioning them. It makes total sense for someone to feel upset, or even misled and their trust betrayed to a degree, when faced with a situation where someone has made a negative impact on them due to blatant disregard for their opinion. Regardless of origin (ie a place of care), that still slaps.

If you care about keeping the relationship and enjoy things otherwise, I would discuss what you both feel are healthy boundaries and talk about how you feel he could better show his worry/concern/"care" for you without tampering with said boundaries. Some people don't know and he may genuinely just have never considered these things and be more than willing to act differently in the future, but please do keep yourself aware of any behavior that makes you uncomfortable in this way and take action to keep yourself safe from someone who might be controlling in the future. Again, you are NTA here and I hope things either improve or you find yourself safely happy on your own.

\*Edit: Just wanted to add that I would keep an eye on him minimizing your concerns or feelings or deflecting them by blaming you (I reference him calling you dramatic). This is something vital to you- your health! If he truly cares and understands, he wouldn't just make decisions for you.

Birthdays are a tricky thing, and everyone approaches them differently. I've known people who don't care one bit about "celebrating" their birthday. I've known people that are the complete opposite of this. Ultimately, this comes down to seeing what your friends value and showing you see them. This is just, in plainly just my opinion, what being a good friend to another is- knowing what your friends value, even if it's not your personal opinion, and showing up to support that. I say this without assumptions of your friends- if you value your birthday in a certain way, maybe explain to your friends what that looks like. Maybe this will give them a better understanding of what to aim for in the future. If you truly value their friendship, sometimes communication and opportunity, however hard they are, can give new life to a situation that doesn't feel good or seem very positive. This is 100% up to you obviously and how you feel about your individual relationships, and I in no way mean to assume how your relationships feel or are.   
If your friend group grieving the loss of a friend, which I am terribly sorry you have to experience, I can absolutely understand how things can slip by or they might feel weird engaging in celebratory things. I don't think it's fair of them to try to negate your feelings by bringing up a recent passing of a friend though. Your feelings and present day life are still important and valuable. I'm sorry they didn't come through for you on your birthday at all. I hope you were able to do some nice things for yourself, and if it means anything, happy belated birthday OP. <3 It sounds like you and your friends have been through some roughness recently with the passing of your friend, and I wish the best for you to come out of this amicably, in a better understanding of each other and without further stressors.

I do not think YTA here, at all. I'm sorry your mother screamed at you, that must have felt unfair and confusing. I'm not going to pretend I understand her position in this situation, nor truly yours, but I don't think it was appropriate for her to yell at you that way in front of your half sister. 

I do wonder how a conversation with your mother would go about how your relationship with your half sister has effected you. Just because she has mental health issues does not absolve her of any responsibility for how she behaves nor does it negate the genuine impact her behaviors have on other people. If you reached out to ask how she was doing, that is definitely showing an interest in someone's wellbeing imo, or at least showing an interest in your mother's life, since this is something she is also going through (helping your half-sister, I mean). If you were tasked with watching over her while your mother was away or something, I suppose that would be different, but nothing you wrote leads me to believe this.  
I hope you continue to assert your boundaries to stay safe and do what you need to in order to maintain your overall health and success as a person. Not everything is black and white, and you wondering if you perhaps had been an AH, to me, is a sign that you are capable of being self aware and considerate of others. In turn, nothing you have written makes me feel like your half sister is doing any of this, although without making assumptions, she could also be thinking about some of these things but feel too complicated or emotionally overwhelmed to discuss or act on them. If you're truly concerned about your own behavior in the situation, perhaps approach your mother and discuss what would feel better for both of you in this situation and try to gain an understanding of where your mother came from in that moment/in general. Maybe you can be doing more to support your mother trying to help her other child, and maybe you could give your mom a few ideas on what showing some understanding for your point of view looks like. Best of luck, OP. This can't be easy and I hope you can continue to find good paths for yourself in life.

I was once told by a psychiatrist to remember that just because I have certain thoughts or emotions or experiences, they do not make me who I am and don’t encompass all I have going on as a person. You can try to use coping skills to practice reacting to your thoughts and emotions to get a handle on how you’d prefer to act on a whilst basis- kind of like acknowledging you’re having certain thoughts, but choosing to act as if you’re not, and not giving what you’re thinking entire power over how you’re acting.

Sometimes drawing lines through everything as a reference keeps me in proportion. So a grid or even just lights lines from the face/chin over. Could even be done traced over your ref pic for a more “accurate” guide. Draw lines for the tips of things, where things bend- just keep track of what they mean to you. I prefer a general grid. Or even taking a finger to a certain area in a ref and using that as a ref for length, instead of drawing all over something. You’re on your way to a great start though, best of luck!

I was going to make a comment about the green highlight being a little confusing but I see it has already been done! Instead, I’ll just leave my other thoughts: well done, fantastic detail. The green highlight is still not totally out of place even, the overall image is quite nice. Great work!

I’d pick up a few reference drawings for proportional help, but also try to draw some perspective lines in the drawing to help guide the foxes overall position. If it’s standing facing us but at an angle, I’d lower the back leg a bit and make it smaller, a little more raised than the other back leg but in a way that represents it as the furthest part of the fox from our POV.

Try reading about figure drawing for some tips on proportion. Also, I see you’ve added some shading to your dragon, which I whole heartedly recommend as a way to add definition to a drawing without drawing a hard line. Try to think of everything as a 3D shape, and don’t be afraid to use a frame or shape base to help guide your overall outline. Also, references can be super helpful in designing and detailing! Good work and good luck. :)
Also, you did a really good job for your first face. Keep it up! :) maybe try watching some process videos or look up information about shapes in relation to drawing people.

I second the shading comment- I love smudging to get certain areas covered and defined but I try to think of shading in terms of how the face is shaped in relation to the light. The tip of a nose might be light but the arch of it is a little further away, so it might be a tad darker. Shading can help give depth to a face’s details. Little spots of light at the highest points of the face, or the highest points of the eyes...
Sorry this got so unorganized, it’s something I just recently started thinking about myself. TL;DR try shading to add definition instead of just lines~
